subject: Polity
description: Article 153-167 — appointment, term, executive, legislative, judicial, discretionary powers

questions.stem: The Governor of a State is appointed by the:
questions.explanation: Article 155 — Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal. NOT elected (unlike the President himself). Holds office during the pleasure of the President (Article 156(1)) — can be removed any time. Term — 5 years (Art 156(3)) or until pleasure withdrawn. Salary fixed by Parliament (Art 158(3)) — currently ~₹3.5 lakh/month. Same person can be Governor of two or more states (7th Amendment, 1956).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The minimum age qualification for being appointed as Governor is:
questions.explanation: Article 157 — qualifications: (1) citizen of India; (2) at least 35 years of age. Article 158 conditions: (i) not a member of Parliament or State Legislature; (ii) not hold any other office of profit. Two unique conventions (not law): the Governor should be from outside the State and major political appointments should follow consultation with the CM (often ignored). The 35-year rule matches the President's age requirement.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following is a 'discretionary' power of the Governor — exercised without aid and advice of the Council of Ministers?

options.option_text: Routine assent to ordinary State Bills
Reserving a State Bill for the President's consideration (Art 200)
Making appointments to the State Public Service
Promulgating ordinances on the CM's advice

questions.explanation: Discretionary powers (constitutional, non-discretionary acts → on CM's advice): (1) Reserving certain State Bills for the President — Art 200 (mandatory if bill threatens HC powers; discretionary otherwise); (2) Recommending President's Rule under Art 356; (3) Discharging functions as Administrator of an adjoining UT (when applicable); (4) Seeking information from the CM under Art 167; (5) Special responsibilities assigned by President (e.g., Art 371 provisions for Maharashtra/Gujarat/Nagaland). All other functions follow the cabinet's advice.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Governor's pardoning power under Article 161 differs from the President's (Art 72) in that the Governor:

options.option_text: Has wider scope than the President
CANNOT pardon a death sentence; CANNOT grant pardon in court-martial cases
Can pardon any offence anywhere in India
Has no pardoning power at all

questions.explanation: Two key restrictions on Article 161: (i) Governor can grant Pardon, Reprieve, Respite, Commutation, Remission for offences against State law — but NOT for death sentences (only President under Art 72 can). (ii) Cannot exercise pardoning power in cases of court-martial. Both Governor and President exercise this power on aid and advice of the Council of Ministers (Maru Ram, Kehar Singh, Epuru Sudhakar judgments). Note: Governor CAN suspend a death sentence to enable a mercy petition to the President.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: An ordinance issued by the Governor under Article 213 must be approved by the State Legislature within:

options.option_text: 30 days from the start of the next session
6 weeks from the start of the next session — else it lapses

questions.explanation: Article 213 — parallel to Article 123 for the President. Ordinance ceases to operate 6 weeks after the State Legislature's reassembly. Effective max life ≈ 6 months recess + 6 weeks ≈ 7.5 months. Must be tabled before the legislature when it reconvenes; can also be withdrawn by Governor any time. Some bill-types require prior instructions from the President before the Governor can issue an ordinance (under State List items reserved for Centre's view). Subject to judicial review.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: When a State Bill is reserved by the Governor for the President's consideration under Article 200, the President can:

options.option_text: Assent, withhold assent, or return the bill (only for non-Money Bills) for reconsideration by the State Legislature
Send it to the Supreme Court for advisory opinion

questions.explanation: Article 201 — three options for the President on a reserved bill: (1) assent; (2) withhold assent (effectively veto, no time-limit — pocket veto possible); (3) direct the Governor to return it (not Money Bill) to the State Legislature for reconsideration; if the legislature passes it again with or without modifications, the President is NOT bound to assent (unlike Parliament's repeat-passage of an ordinary bill returned to Lok Sabha by the President). Note: this triple-tier reservation is a unique federal feature.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Sarkaria Commission (1988) and Punchhi Commission (2010) recommended that the Governor's appointment should:

options.option_text: Be made by the President in consultation with the Chief Minister of the concerned State

questions.explanation: Sarkaria Commission (Centre-State relations, 1988) — recommended (i) Governor should be an eminent person, NOT belonging to ruling party at Centre; (ii) appointment in consultation with the State CM; (iii) fixed term except in extreme cases; (iv) reasoned removal. Punchhi Commission (2010) reaffirmed and added impeachment-like procedure. Most recommendations remain unimplemented; Article 156 still says 'pleasure of the President'. NCRWC (2002) and SC ruling in B.P. Singhal (2010) are related authorities.
